entry.name: CrowdStrike FDR
entry.setup:
1. FDR is a paid Falcon add-on: ask CrowdStrike Support to enable it for your CID if the Falcon console has no
   **Falcon data replicator** page.
2. In the Falcon console, open **Support and resources → Resources → Falcon data replicator** and create a feed.
3. Copy the feed's **access key id**, **secret key** and **SQS queue URL**, and its **S3 path**
   (`s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/`): the bucket is the part between `s3://` and the next `/`.
4. With a feed replicated into your own AWS account, use your queue's URL and bucket and an IAM user allowed
   `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`, `sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility`, `sqs:GetQueueAttributes` on the queue
   and `s3:GetObject` on the bucket.

The queue is read continuously: a notification is deleted only once every event of its files is stored, so nothing

push.instructions:
Fastly streams request logs to an HTTPS endpoint. In the Fastly control panel, open the service's **Logging →
Create endpoint → HTTPS**: **URL** `{{ intake }}/api/v2/logs?ddsource={{ source }}&service=fastly`, **Method**
POST, **Content type** `application/json`, **JSON log entry format** Array of JSON, a **Custom header**
`DD-API-KEY` with the value below, and this **Log format**:

```
{"timestamp":"%{begin:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z}t","message":"%m %U %>s","network":{"client":{"ip":"%h"}},"http":{"method":"%m","url":"%U","status_code":%>s,"useragent":"%{json.escape(req.http.User-Agent)}V","referer":"%{json.escape(req.http.Referer)}V"},"fastly":{"service_id":"%{req.service_id}V","pop":"%{server.datacenter}V","cache_status":"%{fastly_info.state}V","bytes_sent":%B,"duration_us":%{time.elapsed.usec}V}}
```

Fastly first checks the host by fetching `/.well-known/fastly/logging/challenge` from it. The intake answers for
any service unless its operator lists the allowed service ids in `OC_INTAKE_FASTLY_SERVICES` (comma-separated):
then ask them to add this service's id.

entry.setup:
1. In the Fastly control panel, open **Account → API tokens → Create Token**, e.g. `observecraft`, with the
   **global:read** scope (read-only) for all services or the ones to read. Copy it.
2. Leave **Services** empty to read every service the token sees.

entry.description: A GitHub organization's audit log (repositories, members, teams, permissions, settings, Actions, tokens) and its enterprise's audit log as logs, and the open code scanning, Dependabot and secret scanning alerts as metrics.
entry.name: GitHub

push.instructions:
Instead of polling the enterprise audit log, GitHub Enterprise Cloud can stream it: an enterprise owner opens
**Enterprise settings → Audit log → Log streaming → Configure stream → Splunk** and enters:

- **Domain**: the intake's host name (`{{ intake }}` without `https://`)
- **Port**: `443`
- **Token**: the ingest API key followed by `:{{ source }}`, `{{ api_key }}:{{ source }}`
- **Enable SSL verification**: on

GitHub checks and sends to `<Domain>:<Port>/services/collector`, below. Its audit fields (action, actor, repo, …)
are the logs' attributes, as the polled ones. The domain can't carry `?ddsource=` and GitHub sets no source of
its own, so the token's `:{{ source }}` makes them `source:{{ source }}`, as the polled ones, and the GitHub
pipeline and dashboard read them. Turn the **Enterprise audit log** stream off when streaming: one of the two is
enough.

entry.setup:
1. Choose how ObserveCraft signs in:
   - **GitHub App** (recommended): create an app owned by the organization (**Settings → Developer settings →
     GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**), e.g. `observecraft`, without a webhook, with the organization permission
     **Administration: Read** (the audit log) and the repository permissions **Code scanning alerts**,
     **Dependabot alerts** and **Secret scanning alerts: Read**. **Generate a private key** (a `.pem` file) and
     note the App ID; install the app on the organization (all repositories) and note the installation id from
     the installation's URL.
   - **Personal access token**: an organization owner creates a classic token with `read:audit_log`, `read:org`
     and `security_events` (or a fine-grained token on the organization with the same read permissions as the
     app above).
2. The audit log needs GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For the enterprise's audit log, an enterprise owner creates a
   classic token with `read:audit_log` and turns on **Enterprise audit log** below.

**GitHub** hosts an organization's repositories, reviews and Actions. This dashboard reads its audit log (source `github`): repositories created, made public or deleted, members and permissions changed, branch protections removed, tokens and apps; and the open security alerts of its repositories (`github.*.alerts.open`).

Connect an organization in [Integrations → GitHub](/integrations/connectors/github) with a GitHub App.

entry.description: The SSL certificates of a GoDaddy customer (counts by status, days until each expires) and the domains of every certificate with their verification status, read hourly from GoDaddy's API as metrics.

entry.setup:
1. Sign in to the [GoDaddy Developer Portal](https://developer.godaddy.com/keys) and create an API key for the
   **Production** environment; copy the key and its secret (shown once).
2. Find your **customer number** (shopper ID) under **Login Info** on [Login & PIN](https://sso.godaddy.com/security).
3. GoDaddy only opens its production API to some accounts (for example those with 50 or more domains): a 403
   `ACCESS_DENIED` answer means the account has no API access.

entry.setup:
1. Enter your org's Okta domain (`example.okta.com`, `example.okta-emea.com` or a custom domain) and choose how
   ObserveCraft signs in:
   - **OAuth service app** (recommended): in the Admin Console, **Applications → Create App Integration → API
     Services**, e.g. `observecraft`. Under **Client Credentials** choose **Public key / Private key** and add a key
     (Okta can generate one: copy its private key in PEM format and its key id), and turn off **Require
     Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP)**. On **Okta API Scopes** grant `okta.logs.read`, and on **Admin
     roles** assign the **Read-Only Administrator** role. Copy the client id.
   - **API token**: sign in as (or create) an administrator with the **Read-Only Administrator** role, open
     **Security → API → Tokens** and **Create token**; copy it, Okta shows it once. A token unused for 30 days
     expires, and its requests share the administrator's rate limits.

entry.setup:
1. In Temporal Cloud, open **Settings → Service Accounts** and create one, e.g. `observecraft-metrics`, with the

entry.name: Trend Micro Email Security
entry.setup:
1. In the Trend Micro Email Security console, open **Administration → Service Integration → API Access** and
   **Add** an API key (or copy an existing one).
2. On the **Log Retrieval** tab of the same page, enable log retrieval and select the **Mail tracking** and

endpoints.instructions:
Add another drain of type **Traces** for the same projects, with this **Custom Endpoint**, format
**Protobuf** (or JSON) and the header below. Spans arrive as OpenTelemetry traces (APM); logs written during
a traced request carry its `traceId` and `spanId`.
endpoints.label: Traces

push.instructions:
Drains need a Vercel Pro or Enterprise plan.

**Logs.** In Vercel, open **Team Settings → Drains → Add Drain**, choose **Logs**, the projects, sources
(`lambda`, `edge`, `static`, `build`, `external`, `firewall`, `redirect`) and environments, then **Custom
Endpoint**:

- **Endpoint URL**: `{{ intake }}/api/v2/logs?ddsource=vercel`
- **Format**: JSON
- **Custom Headers**: `DD-API-KEY: {{ api_key }}`

Vercel tests the endpoint when the drain is created. Copy the drain's **signature verification secret** below:
the intake then refuses deliveries without a valid `x-vercel-signature`.

push.instructions:
ZIA's traffic logs come from **Cloud NSS** feeds (a Cloud NSS subscription). In the ZIA Admin Portal, open
**Administration → Nanolog Streaming Service → Cloud NSS Feeds → Add Cloud NSS Feed** once per log type (web,
firewall, DNS, tunnel, SaaS security, SaaS security activity, admin audit, endpoint DLP, email DLP):

- **SIEM Type**: Other; **API URL**: `{{ intake }}/api/v2/logs?ddsource={{ source }}&service=zscaler`
- **HTTP headers**: `Content-Type: application/json` and `DD-API-KEY` with the value below
- **Feed Output Type**: JSON, **Feed Escape Character** `,\"`, **Time Zone** GMT
- **Feed output format**: the one this tile's **Overview** shows for the log type, which wraps each record as
  `{"sourcetype": "zscalernss-…", "event": {…}}` for the Zscaler pipeline

Save, then **Activate** the changes.

API Client**, e.g. `observecraft`, with the ZIA role allowed to read the admin audit logs; copy its client id and

instructions below.
